To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) users of software systems have a wide range of information needs, which are not always addressed by bug tracking systems, (2) users are not always able to provide the information that developers need, and (3) users are willing to provide additional information, if they are asked in the right way.

(1) the questions asked in bug reports are often about the status of the bug, and the users want to know when it will be resolved; (2) users often want to help the developers to resolve their bug; (3) users often want the developers to help them to use the software, and (4) the questions asked are often about features that the user wants to see added to the software.
bug reports are a means to improve communication between developers and users, and that bug tracking systems can improve the quality of the communication.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the information needs in bug reports and how they are met.
the information needs of the users and developers of open source software.
understanding how bug reports are used in the development process and with providing practical suggestions for improving the support of this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bug tracking system is not only used to report and fix bugs, but it is also used to communicate between developers and users.
bug reports are not just bug reports, they are information requests.
the users are not just the ones who are reporting bugs but also the ones who are actively participating in solving the bugs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the users of a bug tracking system are not only consumers, they are also producers of information.
bug tracking systems should be more user-centric and should provide better support for the communication between users and developers.
bug tracking tools should be more than just tools for tracking and managing bugs: they should also be tools that support collaboration between developers and users.
The main takeaway from our work is that
developers should be more responsive to the questions users ask in bug reports.
bug tracking systems need to be designed to better support the collaboration between the developers of a system and its users.
bug reporting is a social process that involves the developers and the user in close interaction and that tool support should reflect that.
